newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Red Cross stops Chechnya work after staffers die.
newsitem.headline: Red Cross stops Chechnya work after staffers die.

text.p: The International Committee of the Red Cross confirmed on Tuesday that six Western staff members had been killed in Chechnya on Tuesday and said it had frozen all its work in the breakaway Russian region with immediate effect.

Spokesman Tony Burgener of the Geneva-based humanitarian agency told Reuters the six were murdered in their sleep at their home inside a Red Cross hospital compound in Novye Atagi at four a.m. local time. He did not give their identities, saying families had yet to be informed.
Burgener said the 14 remaining Red Cross staff members at Novye Atagi, 17 km (11 miles) southwest of Chechnya's capital Grozny, would be evacuated on Tuesday, together with the six bodies, he said.
"It was an attack on their residence when they were sleeping at four a.m. this morning. It was an assassination," he said.
"We are strongly condemning this attack, which is a serious violation of international humanitarian law. The hospital was clearly marked with Red Cross signs all over it," Burgener said.
It was the worst attack on ICRC staff since the killing of three Swiss Red Cross staff members in Burundi on June 4.
